lines.t: Hello! Welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
Hi! I'm Sam. Today we talk about birthdays and parties.
Saturday was Aysu's birthday. She is seven now. Happy birthday, Aysu!
I came over to the party. I had a gift, a present, for her.
What was the gift?
A big, red ball. For a dog.
For a dog? Aysu is a girl!
She says she wants to be a dog. She was very happy.
[laugh] And there was a cake. A big cake. My mother said, "Have some cake!"
I sat down and I ate three pieces. Then Aysu looked at me and said, "Sam, that is my cake."
We had music, and we all danced. Even my grandmother. All her friends came too.
I danced with your grandmother. She is fast! She never stops!
Aysu's birthday is a holiday in our family. Nobody goes out. Everybody stays home.
Thank you for coming. Oh, no! Thank you for the party. Happy New Year!
Sam, it is November. [laugh] Bye for now!
Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is celebrations. And Leyla invited me to a traditional Novruz party.
It was Sam's first Novruz. Everybody dressed up, and the guests brought sweets.
I didn't know what to wear. I put on my best shirt, and everyone said, "Why are you dressed for a funeral?"
[laugh] We decorated the table with wheat and eggs. And we put up lights in the garden.
Then at midnight we had fireworks. I jumped over a small fire. It was very exciting.
Did you celebrate? Or did you run away?
I celebrated! Then I ran away. Then I celebrated again. Your uncle said, "Have a great time!"
And you stayed up until four in the morning.
Yes. I ate so many sweets. In the end, I didn't need a present. I needed a doctor.
[laugh] Congratulations, Sam, you survived your first Novruz.
Cheers! Next year I will bring the sweets.
No. Next year you bring the fire.
Deal. See you next time!
Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is festivals, anniversaries and traditions. This week is special: it's my parents' anniversary.
Thirty-five years! What are they doing?
They're having a gathering at home. My dad says, "The more the merrier." So thirty people are coming to a flat for six.
Is there a ceremony?
There's a toast, and a speech by my dad. It lasts twenty minutes. Last year he finished with a salsa dance. Mum wants to paint the town red afterwards.
At sixty-five?
She says her feet are still young. My sister set off a box of fireworks in the garden last time, by mistake.
[laugh] That's a tradition now.
Yes. And the decorations — Mum starts in November. Everything glows.
What about the feast?
Enormous. Last year there were leftovers for two weeks. We sat down and ate up everything on the last day, and then went out for pizza.
In my family, we get together for New Year's Eve and ring in the new year with the whole family, and cards.
Cheating cards.
Of course. A question for our listeners: which celebration is the most important in your family, and why?
My answer: the one with food. See you next time!
